name: PA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+19 partisan lean anchors the race firmly in Democratic territory
Incumbent Brendan Boyle holds a $5.8 million war chest with no outside spending against him
Republican challenger Jessica Arriaga shows no reported fundraising or campaign infrastructure
Prediction markets price Boyle around 96% to win
model.rationale: The D+19 district plus Boyle's incumbency, large financial advantage, and complete absence of visible challenger fundraising all point to an overwhelming Democratic win, and markets agree. With no general-election polling available, uncertainty stays moderately wide, but every directional signal favors Boyle by a wide margin.
model.watch: Any sign of unexpected challenger fundraising, outside spending, or a national environment shifting sharply against Democrats would be the first indication this margin could tighten.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Pennsylvania's 2nd District is strongly Democratic, with a partisan lean of about 19 points, and incumbent Brendan Boyle is seeking another term with every structural advantage intact. He has raised roughly $2.8 million this cycle and holds $5.8 million in cash, with no outside groups opposing him. Republican challenger Jessica Arriaga reports no fundraising on file, and no polls or expert ratings track this race.

Prediction markets price Boyle's chances at about 96 percent, and the underlying fundamentals point to a Democratic margin in the mid-20s. The forecast calls this race Safe Democratic, with Boyle heavily favored to return to Congress. The main open question is only the size of the victory, not which party wins the seat.
